🔊 Envoy: Accepting Tehran’s terms, only path to balanced talks with US

📌 Islamabad, IRNA – Iran’s ambassador in Pakistan underscored the country’s unwavering steadfastness against American bullying and economic terrorism, and said, “If America implements them, accepts them, we are ready to sit down and negotiate with them.”

Speaking in an interview with AsiaOne , Reza Amiri Moghadam said, “Even though they imposed two senseless wars on us, we never walked away from the negotiating table. It was the US and Trump who pulled out of the 2015 JCPOA deal.”
​
Criticizing US anti-Iran measures, especially Donald Trump’s crimes, he said, “We’re not asking much from America. We’re just saying release our funds that you’ve blocked for years. We’re saying end the naval blockade, and we’ll recoup in the Strait of Hormuz.”
​
“We’ve always pursued regional collective security,” he reiterated.
​
Ever since the day of the victory of the Islamic Revolution, Tehran has wanted the region to be run by the countries of the region, the diplomat said.
​
“For eight years America provoked Saddam against us. The Persian Gulf states all backed Saddam during Resolution 598, which brought an end to the Iran-Iraq war and secured a ceasefire. We pushed for and included a clause where Iran plus Iraq plus the six Persian Gulf countries would build regional security together. After that, we presented the Hormuz Initiative to the six Persian Gulf states, proposing that under the banner of Hormuz we form a coalition, solve our issues among ourselves and protect our own regional security.”
​
Commenting on the agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, Amiri Moghadam said, “It has to be clear what the goal behind the agreement is. They’re definitely reviewing it in Iran right now. And if this is meant for security within the region to keep outsiders from meddling in our country, meaning we block Israeli influence, we block American influence, that’s a very good thing.”
